decisions.reason: The paper collects new data in a randomized classroom experiment (Study 2) to re-test the previously published utility value intervention findings, which is a replication.

decisions.quote: Although the research generated by the expectancy-value framework has been largely correlational (Wigfield & Cambria, 2010), recent classroom studies reveal that interventions designed to enhance perceptions of value can increase both interest and course perfor- mance (e.g., Hulleman & Harackiewicz, 2009; Hulleman, Godes, Hendricks, & Harackiewicz, 2010). The research presented herein replicates and extends this prior work by further investigating a theory-based intervention designed to enhance student motivation and performance.

passages.literal_quote:
However, our investigation led to a surprising

finding: instead of further bolstering students’ utility value, as

found in prior research (e.g., Hulleman et al., 2010), the utility

value conditions increased students’ expectancies for success. This

was surprising because our theory and prior research had focused

on perceptions of utility value as the primary mechanism of

intervention effects.
